Subject: Mutual action plan: performance tradeoffs, congestion tests & close timetable

Hi Alex / Priya —

Attaching a concise MAP draft and the proposal timeline for closing by end of July. High-level ask: align on the performance guardrails (latency targets, TTFT, and concurrency behavior) for the pilot so we can finalize SKU + reserved capacity. Key items in the MAP:

- Acceptance targets: p95 latency <= 220ms for 512-token prompt; TTFT <= 65ms for first token on the preferred variant.
- Throughput: sustained 1200 tokens/sec per pod at 16 concurrent sessions for conversational flows.
- Concurrency plan: 3-stage ramp (10%/50%/100%) over 48 hours during canary.
- Variant trade study to include: quality (human preference / accuracy on 200 QA prompts) + perf (latency/TTFT/throughput).

Attachments: map_timeline_v3.xlsx (MAP milestones), initial test checklist.

Can you confirm: (1) these acceptance thresholds look sensible for your use case, and (2) availability for a short review Monday 07/05 to lock the MAP and contract terms?

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Strategic Solutions – Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.ai>, Alex Romero <alex@healthnimbus.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: performance tradeoffs, congestion tests & close timetable

Thanks Mina — I ran an initial perf sweep against three candidate variants from our catalog (we labeled them V-A, V-B, V-C for the experiment). Summary below, full data attached (congestion_test_results.csv).

Summary (avg over 50 runs, 512 tokens, 10 warm-up runs):
- V-A (fp16, high-qual): p50 latency 85ms, p95 260ms, TTFT 72ms, throughput 980 tok/s @ 12 concurrent sessions. Quality: human pref 78/200 = 39%.
- V-B (quant-8, balanced): p50 latency 68ms, p95 210ms, TTFT 58ms, throughput 1250 tok/s @ 16 concurrent. Quality: human pref 69/200 = 34%.
- V-C (q4_0 aggressive): p50 latency 54ms, p95 175ms, TTFT 45ms, throughput 1600 tok/s @ 20 concurrent. Quality: human pref 56/200 = 28%.

Notes: V-B hits the MAP p95 target (<=220ms) and is the best tradeoff for throughput+TTFT while keeping quality degradation modest vs V-A. V-C is excellent perf but the quality drop is noticeable on the 200 QA prompts (common hallucination patterns on multi-step medical instructions).

Attached: congestion_test_results.csv (raw trace + concurrency sweep), nimbus_perf_report_v1.pdf (charts & threshold visualizations). Also included the exact test harness and seed set under Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAP-docs.

Proposed next steps:
1) Customer-directed acceptance test: run V-B on a shadowed slice of production traffic for 48 hours (5% traffic) and collect end-to-end TTFT/p95 and content QA checks.
2) If shadow passes, canary rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours with automatic rollback on perf or QA regression.

I can run the shadow demo as early as Friday 07/02 if you sign off.

—Rishi

From: Alex Romero <alex@healthnimbus.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@healthnimbus.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: performance tradeoffs, congestion tests & close timetable

Mina / Rishi —

Appreciate the quick sweep and clear write-up. The numbers make sense; our main priority is conversational latency + TTFT for clinician workflows. V-B looks like the right compromise. Two asks before we greenlight the shadow test:

1) Can you tighten TTFT to <=60ms if possible? Any kernel or routing knobs we should enable?
2) We need a short report on sample failure modes observed for V-C (the hallucination examples Rishi mentioned) — we'll share with our clinical SME.

If you can get a short note on (1) and the V-C failure examples by EOD 07/02, we can approve the 5% shadow on 07/03 and target contract signature the week of 07/12.

Thanks,
Alex
CTO — Nimbus Health

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: performance tradeoffs, congestion tests & close timetable

Alex —

Quick follow from CS/plans ops:
- Canary cadence recommendation: 10% for 6 hours, monitor p95 & TTFT and sample 500 in-prod responses for QA; if green, 50% for 18 hours; if green, 100% for 24 hours.
- Autoscaling floor: keep 2 extra pods available during canary to avoid transient p95 spikes from cold starts.
- Suggested default routing policy: prefer V-B in region-us-west, fallback to V-C only if V-B capacity exhausted and an explicit lower-quality tolerance is set.

I'll add these items into the MAP doc and push a version to Drive. Also linking our readiness checklist and the DocuSign envelope once Mina and Marissa confirm pricing/credits.

Lauren Bishop
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
